title: Sprite Animation Engine — Runtime Wiring (v1)
why: Entities currently render placeholder rects; the Animation Studio sheet JSONs (frames, bbox, timing) exist in assets but nothing in the game consumes them. The 2026-10-27 session proposed the entity.sprite contract (anchor + anims dict + setAnim) but it was never written down or built.
outcomes: Real sprite frames on entities driven by sheet JSON; uniform per-animation scaling from target height (48px/Y-unit); fixed physical anchor with collision box re-resolution; playback mode/direction/timing per docs/architecture/sprites.md; every entity type wired through one generic setAnim() path.

milestones.name: Sheet Loader
pattern: Port & Adapter (pure data core + DOM adapter)
milestones.objective: Parse Animation Studio _sheet.json into a runtime-ready SpriteData model and load the frame PNGs, with zero game-state coupling.
milestones.success: loadSpriteData() returns frames, bboxes, fps, mode/direction/timing for any sheet path; node-testable without DOM; all 189 petal-panic sheet paths parse.
milestones.diagram:
graph TD
    A[assets levels/enemies */*_sheet.json] --> B[sheetLoader.parseSheet - pure]
    B --> C[SpriteData: anims dict]
    D[browser Image loader] --> E[frame cache keyed by path]
    C --> F[SpriteData ready]
    E --> F

tasks.name: SpriteData model + sheet parser
tasks.what: Add js/core/spriteData.js: pure parse of a _sheet.json into {anims: {name → {fps, mode, direction, timing, frames: [{file, bbox}], collisionBox, pivot}}} plus validation (nonzero source box height, frame count from JSON only).
tasks.why: Single runtime shape every later milestone consumes; keeps Animation Studio JSON as source of truth per sprites.md §2.
acceptance: parseSheet on level1 block_single_sheet.json yields 1 anim with 2 frames and correct bboxes
parseSheet on a platform sheet yields 4 frames
frame count never defaults to 8 — comes from JSON only
zero-height collision box throws

tasks.name: Frame image loader + cache
tasks.what: Add browser adapter loadFrames(spriteData, baseDir) that resolves each frame file to a PNG via new Image(), caches by path, and marks readiness; no-op safe in node.
tasks.why: Separates DOM I/O from the pure model so tests stay headless and images load once per session.
acceptance: loading level1 block_single yields 2 complete images
second call for same sheet returns cache without new Image()

milestones.name: Scale + Anchor Transform
milestones.objective: Implement per-animation uniform scaling from target height and the fixed physical anchor, so sprite and geometry never drift apart.
milestones.success: An entity with 1.0-unit idle and 0.6-unit crouch renders at coherent sizes; anchor stays world-fixed across setAnim; all geometry uses one pipeline: scale → anchor → pivot → mirror → rotate.
milestones.diagram:
graph LR
    A[targetH units x 48px] --> B[scale = targetPx / sourceBoxH]
    B --> C[uniform scalar on frames+boxes+markers]
    C --> D[translate into anchor space]
    D --> E[anchor fixed in world]
    E --> F[pivot / mirror / rotate]

tasks.name: entity.sprite contract + setAnim()
tasks.what: Extend Entity with sprite = {anchor, anims: {name → {sheet|data, targetH, fps?, mode?, timing?}}} and generic loadSprite()/setAnim(name): compute uniform scale (targetH*48 / source box height), re-resolve collision box around the fixed anchor, swap active anim. Keep old this.anim working as fallback.
tasks.why: The 2026-10-27 session contract, now codified; every entity type gets identical behavior from one code path and hand-rolled per-entity scaling dies.
acceptance: setAnim between two targetH values changes rendered size by exactly the ratio, width included (uniform)
entity world position (anchor) is identical before/after setAnim
collision box re-resolves around anchor, no teleport
entity without sprite block still draws legacy rect

tasks.name: Anchor + transform pipeline in draw()
tasks.what: Replace Entity.draw()'s center-pivot translate with the §22 pipeline: uniform scale → translate into physical-anchor space (default bottom-center) → pivot → mirrorX/Y → rotate. Collision box and any per-frame geometry use the same transforms.
tasks.why: One pipeline for sprite AND geometry is the core invariant of sprites.md — rendered art and spatial metadata must never drift apart.
acceptance: mirrored entity keeps collision box symmetric and world-fixed
rotation about pivot moves sprite and its boxes together
bottom-center anchor: feet stay on floor across anim switch

milestones.name: Playback Engine
milestones.objective: Replace the v1 Anim (single speed+loop) with full sprites.md §5–7 playback: per-frame durations, loop/once, forward/reverse/ping_pong(_reverse), and fps vs relative timing.
milestones.success: All four directions traverse correctly with no endpoint duplication; once-completion is exposed for gameplay; relative mode maps [0,1] progress to traversal ignoring per-frame durations.
milestones.diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Playing
    Playing --> Playing : tick dt / setProgress p
    Playing --> Completed : once + terminal frame elapsed
    Completed --> Playing : replay from start

tasks.name: SpritePlayer (mode/direction/timing)
tasks.what: Add js/core/spritePlayer.js implementing §5–7: frame traversal for forward/reverse/ping_pong/ping_pong_reverse, per-frame duration overrides, loop/once with completion flag, and fps vs relative (setProgress 0..1) timing.
tasks.why: The existing Anim class only does constant-speed forward loop; the sheet JSONs already carry mode/direction/timing that must be honored exactly.
acceptance: ping_pong sequence over 5 frames visits 1,2,3,4,5,4,3,2,1,2 with no 5,5 or 1,1
reverse+once completes on frame 1; forward+once on last frame
frame with explicit duration holds longer than 1/fps neighbors
relative: progress 0.5 lands mid-traversal regardless of fps

tasks.name: Wire SpritePlayer into Entity, retire v1 Anim path
tasks.what: Entity.setAnim() now builds a SpritePlayer from the anim's data; tick(dt) advances it; relative-timing anims expose setProgress for gameplay (jump phase mapping later). Keep Anim class for legacy placeholder users until all entities migrate.
tasks.why: One playback implementation everywhere; completion flag lets AI react to 'once' anims per §6.
acceptance: loop anim runs indefinitely; once anim stops and animDone=true after terminal duration
legacy entities using Anim still render (no regression)

milestones.name: First Wiring — Blocks & Platforms
pattern: Vertical slice (data → render → verify in game)
milestones.objective: Render real block/platform art from their sheets through the new engine — the smallest safe first integration, building directly on today's parallax work.
milestones.success: In-game horizontal + vertical areas show real single/double/triple block and platform frames instead of orange rects; collision boxes unchanged; debug view modes still work.
milestones.diagram:
graph TD
    A[block_single/double/triple _sheet.json] --> B[SpriteData + frames]
    C[level def: sprite blocks for solids] --> D[setAnim per width variant]
    B --> E[Entity draw pipeline §22]
    D --> E
    E --> F[render.js solid loop uses entity.draw]

tasks.name: Terrain sprite defs + render integration
tasks.what: Add per-level terrain sprite config (block_single/double/triple, platform_single/double/triple sheet paths + targetH in units) and make the solid/platform draw loop in render.js use entity.draw() with width-variant tiling (5-unit platform = triple+double) instead of fillRect.
tasks.why: First real-sprite vertical slice; validates loader→scale→anchor→playback end-to-end on static art before touching heroes/enemies.
acceptance: horizontal area shows level-themed block art, not orange rects
one-way platforms show platform art as a thin strip anchored to the landing face (R5.1 rule kept)
width > 3 tiles variants without stretching (uniform scale preserved)
collision-only debug mode (viewMode 1) still hides sprites

tasks.name: In-browser visual verification harness
tasks.what: Add a debug spawn/test screen (or extend the existing debug keys) that walks a horizontal + vertical area with real terrain sprites and logs any frame-load failures or scale mismatches.
tasks.why: Headless tests can't see pixels; a quick in-game pass is how we confirm the art actually looks right before wiring heroes.
snippet: // debug: press key → jump to area 1 (horizontal) / vertical area\n// HUD line: 'sprites: 12/12 frames loaded, 0 scale warnings'
acceptance: all terrain frames report loaded in both orientations
no console errors on zone transition with sprites active
verify: manual browser check (documented steps in task)

milestones.name: Geometry Collections (boxes + markers)
milestones.objective: Expose per-frame boxes, point markers, and radius markers as typed collections with world-transformed queries, keeping gameplay logic out of the sprite engine.
milestones.success: getBoxes('melee'), getPoint('beam-origin'), getRadii('explosion') return world-space geometry aligned to the rendered sprite; zero entries are legal; labels need not be unique.
milestones.diagram:
graph TD
    A[frame.boxes / points / radii - typed] --> B[transform pipeline §22]
    B --> C[world-space collections]
    C --> D[gameplay queries by type]
    D --> E[AI / attack patterns interpret meaning]

tasks.name: Per-frame boxes + point/radius markers
tasks.what: Extend SpriteData parsing for per-frame boxes[]/points[]/radii[] (type, position, size/radius) and add Entity query methods returning world-transformed copies: getBoxes(type), getPoint(type), getRadii(type). All use the §22 pipeline; zero entries legal.
tasks.why: Melee damage stays frame-defined (§16) and markers give attack patterns their WHERE without turning JSON into a scripting language (§20).
acceptance: marker world position matches rendered sprite pixel under mirror+rotation
frame with no boxes returns [] not error
duplicate labels both returned (no uniqueness assumption)

tasks.name: Transition safety (clamp-first)
tasks.what: Implement §19: on setAnim, if the new collision box overlaps solids, clamp the anchor along the smallest axis until clear; if no free direction, keep the old box and retry next frame.
tasks.why: Standing up from crouch under a low ceiling must never force penetration — the doc's acceptance test requires it.
acceptance: crouch→stand under low ceiling clamps instead of penetrating
boxed-in entity keeps old box and transitions when space opens

milestones.name: First Wiring — Checkpoint & Barrels
pattern: Vertical slice (data → render → verify in game)
milestones.objective: Render real checkpoint flag and barrel art from their sheets through the new engine — static single-anim entities, the smallest safe first integration.
milestones.success: In-game checkpoints show level/boss flag art (triggered state swaps anim) and barrels show wooden/coin/explosive art; collision boxes unchanged; debug view modes still work.
milestones.diagram:
graph TD
    A[objects/checkpoint + objects/barrel _sheet.json] --> B[SpriteData + frames]
    C[entity defs: sprite blocks, bbox = scale reference] --> D[setAnim per type/state]
    B --> E[Entity draw pipeline]
    D --> E
    E --> F[existing draw loops call entity.draw]

tasks.name: Checkpoint + barrel sprite wiring
tasks.what: Add sprite blocks to checkpoint and barrel entity defs (sheet paths per type/state; frame bbox as scale reference: scale = box.h / bbox.h) and make their draw() use the sprite pipeline with legacy rect fallback until frames load.
tasks.why: First real sprites in-game on static entities — validates loader→scale→draw end-to-end with zero state-machine complexity.
acceptance: checkpoints render flag art sized to their collision box, bottom-anchored
boss-zone checkpoint uses boss flag art
all three barrel types render their own art
collision-only debug mode still hides sprites
